newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican opposition politicians join hunger strike.
newsitem.headline: Mexican opposition politicians join hunger strike.

text.p: Three Mexican opposition lawmakers said they will start a week-long fast on Wednesday in support of two streetsweepers whose hunger strike has become a big embarrassment for President Ernesto Zedillo.

Two federal deputies and a senator will go without food for seven days to pressure Zedillo to help the cleaners, who slipped closer to death on Tuesday after their 92nd day drinking only water and glucose.

Doctors say the two men, lying virtually unconscious under a makeshift tent outside Mexico City's National Human Rights Commission, could die at any moment and have probably suffered irreversible physical and mental damage.

The cleaners are protesting on behalf of 300 colleages from Villahermosa, the capital of the extremely impoverished southeastern state of Tabasco. The cleaners say they were fired for refusing to do unpaid, off-duty jobs for local officials.

The protest has received national attention and cast a spotlight on the dire conditions of some government workers and the plight of the poor in Mexico following its most serious economic crisis in decades.
Senator Felix Salgado and deputy Adriana Luna Parra are from the leftist Democratic Revolutionary Party (PRD), while deputy Mauro Gonzalez Luna is an independent.
Last week, a group of about a dozen men stormed the Mexican Congress and stripped naked before lawmakers in a protest act of support for the hunger strikers.
